claims.head: Like for like: Hertl against Mikheyev
claims.call: The Golden Knights’ L3 (Hertl, Lavoie and Connelly) spends at least 46% of its 5-on-5 time against the Lightning’s third line.
claims.body: At home, the Golden Knights keep sending Hertl’s line (Hertl, Lavoie and Connelly) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Craig keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Lightning’s third line is Girgensons, Holmberg and Mikheyev.

notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 6 of their last 7 games, including the last one. Nikita Kucherov takes shifts on two lines, L1 and L2. Emil Lilleberg is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Hedman and McDonagh.
Yanni Gourde is on the injured non-roster list (hip surgery) and has not played this season. Ilya Mikheyev has taken his spot beside Zemgus Girgensons and Pontus Holmberg.
John Carlson is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, down from 47% with his old team last season.

faceoff.text: Anthony Cirelli is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 41% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 28 seconds at a time, against 67 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Brandon Hagel (9 of 16 changes).

VGK.head: Leaning the Golden Knights’ way
VGK.body: Vegas has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Lightning can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

TBL.head: A slightly uphill night for the Lightning
TBL.body: Vegas has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. The Lightning’s best way to tip it is keeping shots to a minimum.

story.head: Best against best
paras: The Golden Knights have won two in a row, the last a 6-2 rout of Calgary. The Lightning are 5-2-0. Two of the league’s best teams meet.

It’s strength against strength: the Lightning are near the top of the league for shot volume, but the Golden Knights are near the top at keeping shots away. At home, Ryan Craig likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Bolts’ third line.
